item.text: {"text":"Closest architectural match is older than the requested window: [MTAM (CIKM 2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598) introduces temporal gates in recurrent transitions and attention. Its time-aware GRU captures short-term intent, which queries historical memory through time-aware attention—direct precedent for a GRU backbone with jointly trained history retrieval. [TLSRec (CIKM 2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04760) contributes a complementary idea: dimension-wise neural time gates adaptively regulate long- versus short-term preferences using elapsed time. TLSRec itself uses self-attention, so its gating principle would require adaptation to preserve GRU4Rec.\n\nWithin 2023–2026, [TiCoSeRec (AAAI 2023)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/25540) links irregular interaction intervals to preference drift and proposes interval-aware sequence augmentation; it does not establish a new GRU forgetting gate. [MOJITO (SIGIR 2023)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.08158) models temporal context through attention mixtures within a Transformer, providing related temporal-context evidence rather than a compatible backbone replacement. Practical hypothesis inferred from these papers: condition GRU retention on observed inter-event gaps, then let the final valid GRU state query masked historical states through recency-aware attention. Train all components jointly as one model per category; test against the corrected GRU baseline using macro validation HR@10. Use only timestamps available in the observed prefix, never the unknown next-interaction time, and preserve final-nonpadding readout for left-padded histories. These sources motivate the experiment but provide no evidence of gains on this pinned benchmark."}
